artifacts.summary: Confirms the decision-pipeline gap (no obligation field, no validity check) field-for-field against the live source store; reconciles with the adjacent composer feature (premise re-validation) and rules it does NOT already cover a settled route as an acted-on premise (different data source, different claim shape); finds the decisive Owner-ruling precedent (composer emits, receiving agent adjudicates; general conflict detection explicitly excluded in writing) and recommends candidates (1)+(3) over (1)+(2) on architectural-precedent grounds, with the mirror-image fixture folded in as a proposal-time self-check rather than a schema-side check.

memory_candidates.content: This codebase's pattern for adding a new OPTIONAL field to an existing append-only JSON schema (orchestrate-record-decision.sh's .decisions.json writer): branch the jq -c -n record-construction call in two (with-field / without-field), never apply an unconditional `+ {field: $val}` merge, and omit the field entirely (never write an empty string) when its value cannot be computed on the writing host. Demonstrated by the existing `description_fingerprint` field; keeps legacy entries valid and the schema backward compatible.

orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh (the dispatch composer) has an explicit, written Owner ruling (report-format.md, 'Owner ruling -- split by capability'): the composer only EMITS known facts (description text, prior artifact pointers) alongside each other; it never ADJUDICATES whether two claims agree or whether a claim is true. General semantic conflict/validity detection was explicitly rejected for this composer on the grounds that contradiction/validity is a semantic relation between arbitrary spans, not an enumerable pattern. Any future task proposing a composer-side validation step for anything semantic (not just carried figures) should check this precedent first -- it generalizes past the feature it was written for.
